quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When changing lanes, riders should:

options.text: Rely only on their mirrors to identify other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Not worry about other traffic.
Slam on the brakes to allow any vehicles in their blind spot to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic before you change lanes.

questions.question: One way to tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding is if:

options.text: There is a hissing noise coming from the rear of the bike.
The back end is jerking from side to side.
You are unable to accelerate.
The rear brake does not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end is jerking from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually will not hear the tire fail.

questions.question: The control for the rear brake is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: You operate the rear brake with your right foot.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of a lane.
Always avoid the right portion of a lane.
Always avoid the center portion of a lane.
Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whichever portion of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no lane position you always need to avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: Increase your following distance:

options.text: If the roadway is slippery.
If there are only a few vehicles on the roadway.
If the sun is shining.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the roadway is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. This includes slippery pavement, poor visibility, and heavy traffic.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Weave among the three portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to merge back too soon.

questions.question: To help provide space for drivers attempting to merge into your lane from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Merge into the next lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are the ones trying to merge.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Move to a different lane if you can to give them safe space to merge.

questions.question: Why should you use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop?

options.text: Using only one brake will cause the brakes to wear unevenly.
It develops good braking habits for emergency situations.
Using both brakes is the only way to slow down a motorcycle.
The brakes only work when both are applied.

questions.correctAnswerText: It develops good braking habits for emergency situations.
questions.explanation: Using both brakes during normal stops creates a habit you will rely on in emergencies. This habit can be critical when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Is the best way to know that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.
Does not mean that they will yield to you when they should.
Guarantees that they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will yield to you when they should.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but fail to actually see them.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.
Ride faster than usual.
Avoid using your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark. Slow down and increase your following distance when riding at night. Use your high beam whenever you are not meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Cannot tip over.
Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip over if the turn is too sharp or the speed is too fast.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Always slow down.
Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
Accelerate hard.
Not worry about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep your speed steady or speed up slowly while turning.

questions.question: Where should a load be placed?

options.text: As low as possible
As high as possible
Behind the rear axle
On one side of the motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or place them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads on the back of the seat because this raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and affects balance. Distribute loads equally on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks that cross your lane at an angle, it is usually:

options.text: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Dangerous to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
Not safe to cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Safest to cross the tracks by riding on the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safest to ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: When approaching angled railroad tracks, ride straight across them while staying in your lane. Turning to cross the tracks at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could enter another lane of traffic.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated by:

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and use your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see traffic around you before changing lanes.

questions.question: To effectively protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of a soft material.
Be made of a heavy material.
Fit loosely enough that they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some parts of the legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of a heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or another sturdy material that cover your entire legs. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it restricts your movement.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders who have operated their motorcycles for less than six months.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Occur because of distractions caused by passengers.
Happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders who have operated their motorcycles for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when riding a motorcycle that is new to you. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders who have less than six months of experience on that particular motorcycle.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives the most space between you and other vehicles.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives the most space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Choose the position that gives you the most space cushion and helps other drivers see you clearly.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:

options.text: Far from home.
On short trips.
On long rides.
Several hours into the ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: A passenger should never:

options.text: Wear a helmet.
Lean when the operator leans.
Wear clothing that is tight.
Ride sidesaddle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride sidesaddle.
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should wear snug clothing so nothing catches on the motorcycle. They must always lean with the operator during turns. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Incorrect tire pressure.
Brakes that are not working properly.
A balanced load.
Excessive wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Incorrect tire pressure.
questions.explanation: Most wobbles are caused by improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not provide enough eye protection. Use goggles or a face shield instead for proper protection.

questions.question: An advantage to keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You will have a narrow view of the road so you can stay focused.
You will have more time to react to the movements of others.
You can more easily follow the path of the next vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to react to the movements of others.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more space to maneuver.
